claim: BONUSV is the DIP increment table: four .WORD entries, hex under .RADIX 16, whose BCD digit pairs (0100/0120/0150/0200) are scaled *100 to the bonus-life options 10,000/12,000/15,000/20,000
The bonus increment is DIP-selected from OPTNS bits D4-D5 (masked with hex 30) — not modelled by the clone, which hardcodes the first entry
BONUS1 returns the low byte of the selected BONUSV word as the increment
INIT seeds the FIRST threshold from the SAME BONUSV entry it uses as the increment, so the first bonus life lands at the increment itself
The threshold compare runs with decimal mode CLEARED — packed BCD orders identically to binary, so the magnitude test is a plain 16-bit compare
The compare's low byte is SCORE1 against BONUSL — the score's hundreds and thousands digits, so the test has 100-point granularity and never reads SCORE0
The compare's high byte is SCORE2 against BONUSM, completing a two-byte (four BCD digit) comparison of the score in units of 100
A score below the threshold branches away with no award and no advance
The threshold ADVANCE runs in decimal mode — the increment is added to BONUSL:BONUSM as packed BCD
The high byte of the increment is added to BONUSM to set the next bonus level; the carry out of BONUSM has nowhere to go, so the level wraps at four BCD digits

source.verbatim: LDA Y,BONUSV+1		;SET NEXT BONUS LEVEL FOR THIS PLAYER

claim: The OPTSW2 timed-play branch: with the unlimited-time default the award proceeds directly to the lives test (the branch itself is out of the clone's scope)
The award ceiling is 6, tested against LIVES
At six the award is refused — but the threshold has ALREADY been advanced above, so a refused bonus still moves the level
Finding LIVES above six hangs the program in a one-instruction loop (a deliberate watchdog reset), so six is an invariant rather than a clamp
The award itself is a single INC of LIVES

source.verbatim: INC X,LIVES-1		;ADD A LIFE AS A BONUS

claim: The bonus-life sound is a write to CHAN4 — deferred to the cp5 audio epic, not modelled here
LIVES counts SPARE lives, not total: INIT stores NLIVES-1 because the gun on screen is the life being played

source.verbatim: STX LIVES		;NUMBER OF LIVES-1 (WE ARE PLAYING WITH ONE)

claim: DLIVES draws at most six gun icons, matching the six-spare ceiling exactly
A DIFFERENT routine on the same carry: crossing a 10,000-point boundary (the carry out of SCORE1) triggers the new-head frequency bump, not the bonus life
That 10,000-point boundary decrements COUNT3 to increase the frequency of new heads — a separate difficulty dial the clone does not yet model

source.verbatim: STA X,COUNT3-1		;INCREASE FREQUENCY OF NEW HEADS

claim: SCORNG's tail falls straight through to its exit after one award: one scoring event advances the threshold at most once, with no catch-up loop
